one_month_reasoning: The one big event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings, expected about Oct 22 after the close (MarketBeat; not yet confirmed in Intel's IR list). Guidance is $15.8-16.8B revenue, 42% non-GAAP gross margin and $0.38 non-GAAP EPS. Consensus has moved to about $16.72B and $0.39, near the top of the range, so the bar is high. Intel has beaten its own guidance seven quarters running, and Q2 came in $1.8B above the midpoint. Management says it is supply-constrained, especially on substrates and memory, so upside is capped by supply. The Q4 guide and early 2027 capex wording (CFO: 'significantly above' 2026) will set the move. The Intel 14A 0.9 PDK is due in October and could bring customer headlines. INTC has a history of 10-20% moves on earnings. The stock is up about 40% in September and has already pulled back once from about $142 to under $114. Momentum and reversal roughly cancel out. So I center the distribution on about $119 with a slight downward tilt for a high-bar print after a big run. I use a fat-tailed spread (a 70/30 mix of 16% and 30% one-month sigmas), wider than annual vol/3.5 alone, because earnings fall in the window.

fair_value.method: I blend three methods. Forward P/E: 2028E EPS of $2.75 x 35x = $96. EV/NTM sales: 2028E revenue of $80B x 7x, less net claims = $102. SOTP: products business 2027E operating income of $26B, taxed and capitalized at 25x, plus $60B for the foundry option and the Mobileye stake, less debt and NCI = $110. Weighted 40/30/30, that gives about $102 per share on about 5.40B diluted shares, after the August 2026 $23B equity raise.

inputs_detail.derivation: $2.06 grown about 33%. Consensus 2027 EPS growth is about 36% (src 11). Management targets gross margin moving from low-40s to mid-40s and then high-40s (src 8). Foundry losses (about $2.1-2.5B/quarter, src 7, 8) narrow toward the internal breakeven target of end-2027 (src 8). The extra shares from the August raise are already in the consensus base.

Today it trades at 62x 2027 EPS. NVDA is at 28x and TSMC has averaged about 23x over ten years (src 12). I put 35x between peers and today's multiple: growth is still above peers and estimates are being revised up sharply (2027 EPS +35% in 90 days, src 11), but the premium should shrink as supply catches up.

5,043M outstanding at 6/27/26, plus 242.1M offering shares (base plus greenshoe), plus about 119M unvested RSU/PSU, rounded. I exclude the 241M DoC warrants because they are exercisable only if Intel's foundry ownership falls below 51%.

Today it is about 10.4x sales. The past-decade range is 1.5-12.5x (src 13). I assume partial mean reversion as margins stay in the 40s, below the mid-50s-plus margins of peers.

Add the Arizona SCIP NCI of $13.4B. Subtract the 77% Mobileye stake, about $7B (judgment). Net is about $10B.

inputs_detail.derivation: The H1 2026 run-rate of about $17.8B rises to roughly $20B for full-year 2026 as DCAI grows 59% y/y (src 1). Add about 30% for 2027 from supply growth and ASP-per-core stability (src 8).
In line with large-cap semi peers (NVDA 28x, TSMC ~23x average, src 12).

Foundry loses about $2.5B a quarter today (src 8), and external revenue was only $293M in Q2 (src 7). Eight hyperscalers and chip designers are evaluating 14A but none has committed (src 14). I value it as a strategic option rather than on cash flows.

bear.story: Supply catches up in 2027, and the agentic-AI CPU demand narrative cools or shifts to Arm and AMD. Client pricing actions reverse. No 14A anchor customer is named, so the 14A economics are questioned, as management itself warned. 2027 capex well above $20B pushes FCF negative again. EPS lands around $2.0 and the multiple compresses to 30-35x.

base.story: Intel keeps beating guidance while supply-constrained. Gross margin moves into the mid-40s, and CY2028 EPS of about $2.9-3.0 becomes visible. One or two partial 14A or EMIB-T packaging engagements are disclosed. The multiple shrinks from 62x toward about 38-40x forward, so the stock roughly holds.

bull.story: A major 14A anchor customer (Apple, Nvidia or a hyperscaler) is announced around the PDK 0.9 / late-2026 decision window. Server CPU attach rates rise with agentic AI. EMIB-T packaging adds billions per customer from H2 2027. Foundry reaches breakeven by end-2027. CY2028 EPS is above $4 at about 45x.

thesis_break_reason: At $72 the stock would be about 24% below the August 2026 offering price of $95, which is also where the CEO bought $10M of stock. It would be about 35x consensus 2027 EPS, roughly a peer multiple, meaning the market had stopped paying for growth. A move there most likely means the supply-constrained AI-CPU upcycle has turned (guide-down or pricing reversal) and/or 14A has failed to sign an external anchor. Ordinary 76%-vol noise is less likely to explain it.

How long supply constraints and pricing power last once Intel 3/18A and substrate supply grows
Cash needs from 2027 capex well above $20B versus OCF, and the risk of more dilution after the $23B August raise
Whether agentic-AI CPU demand is structural or a narrative peak after a +40% month
reasoning: Primary documents. The Q2 2026 release and 10-Q show revenue of $16.1B (+25% y/y), DCAI +59%, non-GAAP gross margin of 41.8% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.42. GAAP results are distorted by a $13.6B mark-to-market loss on escrowed government shares and a $3.9B Mobileye goodwill impairment. Foundry lost $4.5B in H1. Intel paid Apollo $14.2B for its Ireland SCIP stake. The 424B5 and 8-K show a $23B equity raise at $95 in August (242M new shares, ~4.8% dilution), and a Form 4 shows the CEO bought $10M of it. On the Q2 call and at the Deutsche Bank conference, management said supply, not competition, is the limit through 2028. They gave 2027 capex as 'significantly above' 2026, foundry breakeven targeted for end-2027 with possible slip to 2028, 14A defect density at 22nm-like levels, and the 0.9 PDK due in October. Valuation. Consensus 2027 EPS of $2.06 puts the stock at 58-62x. My three methods give $96-110 and blend to $102, below the $120 price but close to the $116 consensus PT. Base rates. 76% realized vol and a +258% year imply a very wide distribution, and stocks after parabolic runs often mean-revert partially. Strong upward revisions and the 14A optionality offset some of that. I built a three-scenario lognormal mixture: $65/30%, $115/45%, $185/25%, each with 25-33% dispersion. That puts the median at about $111, with P(>=120) at 44%. I fattened the upside tail slightly for a 14A anchor win. Research limits: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data estimate endpoints were paywalled. Consensus figures come from press summaries. I found no relevant Intel prediction market.
